Plot fitted variables

Source: R/plot_tables.r
plot.ecodive_envfit.Rd

Draws the variables that envfit() fitted onto an ordination: an arrow for each numeric variable (or feature), pointing the way it increases, with a length proportional to \(\sqrt{r^2}\), and a label at the centroid of each factor level. With add = TRUE, they go on top of an ordination plot, such as plot(ord).

Usage

# S3 method for class 'ecodive_envfit'
plot(x, add = FALSE, axes = c(1, 2), p_max = 1, col = "blue3", ...)

Arguments

x

The result of envfit().

add

Whether to add to the current plot, such as plot(ord) of the ordination that x was fitted to (TRUE), or start a new one (FALSE, the default).

axes

Which two of x's axes to draw, by number among them. Default c(1, 2).

p_max

Draw only the variables with a p_value at most p_max. Default 1: all of them (including those with no p-value).

col

The colour of the arrows and labels.

...

With add = FALSE, passed on to graphics::plot.default(), such as main, xlab, xlim or asp.

Value

x, invisibly.

Details

The arrows are scaled to fit the plot: with add = TRUE, the longest reaches 80% of the way from the origin to the nearest edge of the plot; with add = FALSE, 80% of the way to the furthest centroid (or they keep their own lengths, \(\sqrt{r^2}\) at most 1, when there are no centroids). Only their directions and relative lengths have meaning, as in any biplot. The centroids are in the ordination's units, so they are drawn where they are. Factor levels are labelled with the level, or with the row name (the variable and the level pasted together) when two variables share a level's name.

Examples

    ord <- pcoa(bray(iris[, 1:4]))
    fit <- envfit(ord, iris, permutations = 99)

    plot(ord, 'Species', iris)
    plot(fit, add = TRUE)


    # On their own.
    plot(fit)
